By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-2t=3 \\ -s+4t=-7 \\ 3s-3t=3\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -7 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-2t=3 \\ t=-2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=-2.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-2t & =3 \\ s-2(-2) & =3 \\ s+4 & =3 \\ s & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-1,\,t=-2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-b-2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-1)\cdot (-2)=2.$
